On Wed, Jan 20, 2027 at 9:43 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> We're looping in Diego (engineer) to attempt reproduction and Monica from CS to track impact and the support ticket.

Thanks — I pulled the example request and reran it against our hosted variant (redwood-large-instruct, v1.2.0) using the same sequence length and prompt. I executed 200 iterations across the same hour range and did not observe empty completions.

What I did find:
- No 500/502/504 errors in platform logs for the request window.
- A small number of transient connection resets were retried by our edge (0.03% of requests in that window). Those retries would normally be retried by client SDKs and surface as a second attempt.
- I correlated request logs using timestamps and couldn't find a request-id matching 2027-01-20T16:11:36Z or 19:02:12Z in the primary shard; it's possible the customer request header did not include an X-Request-ID.

Attached is a redwood request log excerpt for the broader window: redwood-request-log-20270120.txt (contains anonymized request-ids and edge response codes).

Next steps for us:
1) If Helios can provide the X-Request-ID or the exact Authorization token suffix used at the timestamp, we can do a more precise lookup.
2) If we still can't correlate, we'll ask Helios to capture a raw HTTP trace (or enable SDK debug logs) to rule out client-side behavior (retries, truncated payloads).

I'll keep digging, but at this point there's no direct evidence of a platform-wide model blank-output bug.

—Diego

Subject: Re: Observed empty completions from Redwood — sample and timestamps (CLOSURE)

Hi Alex — quick closure note from our investigation. I wanted to summarize findings and recommended next steps so your team has a single reference: 

Summary of investigation:
- Diego correlated Helios-provided client request-ids against Redwood platform logs and did not find matching server-side request-ids or any 5xx errors in the windows you reported.
- Platform traces show a low rate of transient connection resets at the edge during that day; those are typically retried automatically by our edge or client SDKs.
- The Helios-provided client trace indicates an empty HTTP response body observed on the client after an otherwise successful 200 response. We could not reproduce this behavior from the hosted API in controlled tests.

Conclusion:
- At this time we have no platform-side evidence that shows a systemic "empty completion" bug. The most likely explanations are: (a) an intermediary truncation on the client side or in Helios' network, (b) an outdated/custom SDK behavior that discards bodies on certain retry logic, or (c) rare edge-level transient that was not recorded with an associated server request-id.

Recommendations for HeliosHealth:
- Please upgrade to the latest Redwood SDK (we released a retry/connection hardening patch in v2.4.1).
- If possible, enable full client SDK debug logs for the timeframe and re-run the failing requests; share the raw HTTP trace via the support ticket linked below.
- If you capture a server-side X-Request-ID from the future incident, forward it and we'll run a precise correlation within minutes.

Follow-up: Monica from CS will keep the ticket open for another 7 days and will mark as resolved if no new occurrences are reported. If this resurfaces, we'll escalate immediately and can open an infra-level audit.
